newsitem.title: FRANCE: TENNIS-AGASSI CRASHES OUT IN PARIS OPEN SECOND ROUND.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-AGASSI CRASHES OUT IN PARIS OPEN SECOND ROUND.

text.p: Andre Agassi, the winner in 1994, crashed out of the Paris Open when Swede Magnus Gustafsson beat him 6-4 3-6 6-3 in the second round on Tuesday.
The ninth-seeded American was the third seed to go out on the first day that the 16 seeds, given a bye in the opening round, joined the action.
Wimbledon champion Richard Krajicek of the Netherlands and Agassi's compatriot Jim Courier were the other seeded casualties.
The defeat virtually ended Agassi's chances of qualifying for the ATP Tour World Championship in Hanover next month.
"I was just thinking about my game. I wasn't worring about the World Championship," said Agassi.

Eight players qualify for the Hanover event and Agassi is currently in seventh place. But he confirmed he would not be playing another tournament this season, leaving the way open for others to overtake him.
Agassi appeared to have taken control when he came back from a set down to win the second set and go 3-1 up in the third.
The American benefited from a dubious line call in the sixth deuce of the fourth game as he avoided being broken by the Swede.
But Gustafsson, ranked 28, came back strongly to win his next service to love.
He then broke Agassi in the American's next two service games and served for the match, taking it on the first match point when Agassi's baseline drive was long.
Referring to his Olympic gold medal in Atlanta in August, Agassi said: "It's strange to have won something so special in a year in which I have struggled so much."

American Michael Chang, the second seed, was pushed to the limit by Australian Mark Philippoussis before eventually winning their second round clash 7-5 3-6 7-6 and narrowly avoiding the fate of the three other seeds.
Krajicek, the seventh seed, was knocked out 3-6 6-1 7-5 by Alberto Berasategui of Spain after suffering stomach pains, while number 15 Courier lost 6-4 7-5 to Frenchman Arnaud Boetsch.

Philippoussis, whose season had peaked with his first tournament victory in Toulouse two weeks ago, hit 25 aces to Chang's 15. He also hit the fastest serve of the Bercy tournament so far, timed at 205 kph (127 mph).
The big Australian, who turns 20 next week, gave as good as he got in the rallies, making Chang work hard for his points.
Chang had looked like winning comfortably after taking the opening set with the first break of serve in the 12th game.
But it wasn't until two and a half hours later that he finally clinched the match with his third match point of the third set tiebreak which he won 9-7.
Krajicek's loss jeopardised his chances of a place in the ATP Tour World Championship.
There are three places still to be settled and the Bercy tournament results will be decisive.
